name: Jason Statham
milestone_by_age_26: Competed for England in three diving events at the 1990 Commonwealth Games in Auckland as a member of Great Britain's national diving team.
early_history_summary: Statham discovered diving as a young teen after seeing a high dive in Miami and joined a swimming club at age 11-12, quickly making the British team. He spent 12 years on Great Britain's National Swimming Squad, training daily and competing internationally, including Olympic trials for Seoul 1988 and Barcelona 1992.
family_context_summary: Born to dancer Eileen and street seller Barry Statham in Shirebrook, Derbyshire; working-class family where father worked odd jobs as house painter, coal miner, and market stall seller.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in diving or athletics; father was a street seller and mother a dancer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: national diving team, early specialization, daily training
evidence_summary: Statham grew up in a working-class family in Great Yarmouth and discovered diving at age 11-12 after a holiday in Miami. He joined a swimming club and within a year was on the British team, spending 12 years on the national squad. He competed at the 1990 Commonwealth Games in Auckland, finishing 8th in 1m springboard and 11th in 3m and 10m events. He also participated in Olympic trials for 1988 and 1992 but did not qualify. His diving career provided discipline and physical training that later translated into his action film career, beginning with Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels in 1998.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Shirebrook, Derbyshire; father was a street seller and odd-job worker, mother was a dancer.
current_position: One of Hollywood's highest-grossing action stars with films totaling over $8.5 billion worldwide; engaged to model Rosie Huntington-Whiteley; estimated net worth ~$90 million.

name: Khalil al-Wazir
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded the Palestinian National Liberation Movement (Fatah) in November 1959 in Kuwait, serving as a member of its first central committee.
early_history_summary: Al-Wazir became a refugee at age 13 when his family was expelled from Ramla in 1948. He joined the Muslim Brotherhood in Gaza at age 17 and organized military cells conducting operations against Israeli targets by age 20. After moving to Kuwait, he and Yasser Arafat agreed to form a secret liberation organization, formally established as Fatah in November 1959.
family_context_summary: Born to a Muslim family in Ramla, Palestine; father Ibrahim al-Wazir worked as a grocer. The family was expelled in 1948 and settled in the Bureij refugee camp in Gaza.
parent_family_domain_summary: No documented family background in political or military organizing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: refugee, displacement, Palestinian nationalism, armed struggle, Arafat partnership
evidence_summary: Al-Wazir was born in Ramla to a grocer's family and became a refugee at 13 when expelled during the 1948 war. He settled in Gaza, joined the Muslim Brotherhood at 17, and organized military cells by 20, conducting operations against Israeli targets. In Kuwait, he partnered with Arafat to co-found Fatah in November 1959, becoming a member of its first central committee. His refugee experience and direct exposure to the Palestinian displacement crisis were the driving forces behind his political mobilization.
starting_point: Born to a Muslim family in Ramla, Palestine; father was a grocer; family became refugees in 1948 and settled in Bureij refugee camp in Gaza.
current_position: Assassinated by Israeli commandos at his home in Tunis on April 16, 1988, at age 52; final role: deputy to the General Commander of the forces of the Palestinian Revolution and architect of the First Intifada.

trajectory.event: Joined the Muslim Brotherhood in Gaza and became secretary of its student branch.

name: Pierre Bourdieu
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Bourdieu passed the agrégation in philosophy in 1954 and was teaching at a lycée and serving in the military by age 26, but his first major published works emerged from Algeria fieldwork in the late 1950s.

He passed the agrégation in 1954, taught at a lycée in Moulins, and was conscripted into the French Army in 1955, serving in Algeria where he began his sociological fieldwork.
family_context_summary: Born in Denguin, a remote mountain village in southwestern France; father was a postal worker (and former sharecropper). Household spoke Béarnese, a Gascon dialect.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in academia or sociology; father was a postman and former sharecropper.
evidence_summary: Bourdieu was born to a postal worker in a remote Pyrenean village and rose through the French educational elite system, attending Lycée Louis-le-Grand and then the École Normale Supérieure. He passed the agrégation in philosophy in 1954 at age 24 and taught briefly before military service in Algeria. While the agrégation is a prestigious qualification, his first major sociological publications emerged from Algeria fieldwork in the late 1950s and early 1960s, after age 26. No material public milestone by 26 was identified.

name: Mathias Rust
milestone_by_age_26: Flew a rented Cessna from Helsinki to Moscow on May 28, 1987, evading Soviet air defenses and landing on Bolshoy Moskvoretsky Bridge next to Red Square, a globally reported event that led to the dismissal of the Soviet defense minister.
early_history_summary: Rust developed an obsession with flying and politics as a teenager in West Germany. He started taking flying lessons at a local club near Hamburg and accumulated about 50 hours of flying time. At 18, he rented a Cessna, told his parents he was touring northern Europe for flight hours, and instead flew through Soviet air defenses to land in Red Square.
family_context_summary: Born in Wedel, Schleswig-Holstein, West Germany; middle-class family able to support flying lessons. Could not become a commercial pilot due to eyesight deficiency.
parent_family_domain_summary: No documented family background in aviation or politics.
primary_early_advantage_tags: flying lessons, Cessna rental, Cold War, Red Square, solo operation
evidence_summary: Rust grew up in Wedel, West Germany, and developed passions for flying and politics. He took flying lessons at a local club near Hamburg, accumulating about 50 hours of experience. On May 28, 1987, at age 18-19, he rented a Cessna and flew from Helsinki through Soviet air defenses to land on Bolshoy Moskvoretsky Bridge next to Red Square. The event was globally reported and led to the dismissal of the Soviet defense minister and air defense commander, aiding Gorbachev's reforms. He was sentenced to four years but released after 14 months.
starting_point: Born in Wedel, Schleswig-Holstein, West Germany to a middle-class family; could not pursue commercial aviation due to eyesight deficiency.
current_position: Living a private life; reportedly worked as a financial analyst in Switzerland and later as a yoga teacher; has had legal troubles including a stabbing conviction; believed to be residing in Germany or Estonia.

name: Sonal Mansingh
milestone_by_age_26: Performed her arangetram (formal debut) in Mumbai in 1962 and began her professional dance career, with her first performance in Madras at the Museum Theatre the same year.
early_history_summary: Mansingh started learning Manipuri dance at age 4 and Bharatanatyam at age 7. Despite family opposition, she ran away from home at 18 to Bangalore to train under Prof. U.S. Krishna Rao and Chandrabhaga Devi. She performed her arangetram in Mumbai in 1962 and began her professional career, later starting Odissi training under Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra in 1965.
family_context_summary: Born in Mumbai to Arvind and Poornima Pakvasa; grandfather Mangal Das Pakvasa was a freedom fighter and one of the first five Governors of India. Grew up in Raj Bhavans (governor's residences) with exposure to prominent artists.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was artistic; grandfather was a governor and freedom fighter; family hosted prominent musicians and dancers at home, providing early cultural immersion.
primary_early_advantage_tags: guru training, arangetram, Bharatanatyam, Odissi, cultural family, ran away from home
evidence_summary: Mansingh was born into a prominent Indian family with a grandfather who served as governor and a mother who was artistic. She grew up surrounded by prominent artists like Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, M.S. Subbulakshmi, and Rukmini Devi who performed at her home. She started dance at age 4 and Bharatanatyam at 7. At 18, despite family opposition, she ran away to Bangalore to train under Prof. U.S. Krishna Rao. She performed her arangetram in Mumbai in 1962 and began her professional career, later training in Odissi under Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra from 1965.
starting_point: Born in Mumbai to a prominent family; grandfather was a freedom fighter and one of India's first five governors; grew up in Raj Bhavans with exposure to leading artists.
current_position: Nominated Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) from 2018 to 2024; Padma Vibhushan awardee (2003); founder of Centre for Indian Classical Dances; continues to perform and teach at age 81.

name: Vitor Belfort
milestone_by_age_26: Won the UFC 12 Heavyweight Tournament in 1996 at age 19, becoming the youngest fighter to score a victory and win a tournament in the UFC.
early_history_summary: Belfort started boxing at age 12 under Claudio Coelho in Rio de Janeiro. At 17, he won the Brazilian National Jiu-Jitsu Championships (absolute and heavyweight for blue belts under 18), catching the eye of Carlson Gracie, who invited him to train with his elite team. At 19, Belfort moved to the US and made his MMA debut at SuperBrawl 2 in Hawaii, winning by KO in 12 seconds, then won the UFC 12 Heavyweight Tournament.
family_context_summary: Born and raised in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; family details not extensively documented. Moved to the US at 19 with his mother and sister to compete.
parent_family_domain_summary: No documented family background in martial arts or combat sports.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Carlson Gracie, BJJ, boxing, UFC, Rio de Janeiro, phenom, early specialization
evidence_summary: Belfort grew up in Rio de Janeiro and started boxing at 12 under Claudio Coelho. At 17, he won the Brazilian National Jiu-Jitsu Championships, attracting Carlson Gracie who invited him to train with his elite team alongside champions like Murilo Bustamante and Wallid Ismail. At 19, Belfort moved to the US, won his MMA debut at SuperBrawl 2 in Hawaii by KO in 12 seconds, and then won the UFC 12 Heavyweight Tournament, becoming the youngest UFC fight and tournament winner. His explosive knockout power and BJJ skills earned him the nickname 'The Phenom.'

name: Mirosław Hermaszewski
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Hermaszewski graduated from the Polish Air Force Officer School in Dęblin in 1965 at age 24, but his historic spaceflight aboard Soyuz 30 occurred in 1978 at age 37.
early_history_summary: Hermaszewski survived the Volhynian massacre as a toddler and was deported to Wołów after WWII. He developed an interest in aviation, completed a gliding course in 1960, entered the Polish Air Force Officer School in Dęblin in 1961, and graduated in 1965. He was selected for the Interkosmos program in 1976 and flew to space in 1978.
family_context_summary: Born in Lipniki (now Ukraine) to a Polish peasant family; father was killed by the Ukrainian Insurgent Army in 1943 when Hermaszewski was 18 months old. Family was deported to Wołów after WWII.
parent_family_domain_summary: Peasant farming family; no aviation or military background documented.
evidence_summary: Hermaszewski was born in 1941 in Lipniki to a Polish peasant family and survived the Volhynian massacre as an infant, losing his father. After WWII, the family was deported to Wołów. He developed an interest in aviation, completed gliding training in 1960, and entered the Polish Air Force Officer School in Dęblin in 1961, graduating in 1965 at age 24. While this was a professional qualification, his historic milestone—becoming the first Pole in space aboard Soyuz 30—occurred in 1978 at age 37, well after age 26.

name: Josef Němec
milestone_by_age_26: Won a bronze medal at the 1957 European Amateur Boxing Championships in the heavyweight division, establishing himself as one of Czechoslovakia's top boxers.
early_history_summary: Němec took up boxing at age 15 in České Budějovice following his father and two older brothers. He was selected for the national team and called up for military service at ÚDA Praha, where he trained under Olympic champion Július Torma. He competed at the 1956 Olympics and won European bronze medals in 1957 and 1959.
family_context_summary: Born in České Budějovice, Czechoslovakia; father was a laborer and amateur boxer known as 'Táta Němec,' mother was from a confectioner's family. Eight children in the family; father boxed at fairs to earn extra money.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a well-known local boxer; two older brothers also boxed, providing direct family-domain immersion in the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: boxing family, father boxer, ÚDA Praha, Július Torma, national team
evidence_summary: Němec was born in České Budějovice to a laborer's family with deep boxing roots—his father was a local boxing legend and two older brothers also boxed. He started boxing at 15 and was selected for the national team, training at ÚDA Praha under Olympic champion Július Torma. He competed at the 1956 Olympics (quarter-finals) and won European Championship bronze medals in 1957 and 1959, establishing himself as a top European heavyweight. He won 308 of 320 bouts in his career and was nine-time national champion.
starting_point: Born in České Budějovice, Czechoslovakia to a laborer's family; father was a well-known local boxer and mother was from a confectioner's family; eight children.
current_position: Died on September 10, 2013 in České Budějovice at age 79; final role: president of Budweiser Samson Boxing Club and youth boxing coach.

name: Isao Inokuma
milestone_by_age_26: Won the gold medal in the heavyweight division (above 80 kg) at the 1964 Summer Olympics in Tokyo, defeating all three opponents before the final and winning the gold medal match by yusei.
early_history_summary: Inokuma was born in Yokosuka, Kanagawa, and took up judo at age 15 under Riichiro Watanabe. Despite his small size for the heavyweight division, he mastered ippon seoi nage and tai otoshi techniques suited for shorter judoka. He also became a bodybuilder, gaining enough strength to bench press 140kg. He won the 1963 All-Japan Championships before winning Olympic gold in 1964.
family_context_summary: Born in Yokosuka, Kanagawa, Japan; family background not extensively documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: judo, ippon seoi nage, bodybuilding, All-Japan Championships, Olympic gold, Japan
evidence_summary: Inokuma was born in Yokosuka and started judo at 15 under Riichiro Watanabe. Despite being small for the heavyweight division, he mastered techniques suited for shorter judoka (ippon seoi nage, tai otoshi) and supplemented with bodybuilding to bench press 140kg. He won the 1963 All-Japan Championships at age 25 and Olympic gold at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics at 26, defeating his first three opponents by ippon before winning the final by yusei. He also won the 1965 World Championship. His training partner Tōru Mori helped him develop through constant sparring.

current_position: Died on September 28, 2001 in Tokyo at age 63; reportedly committed suicide; final role: president of Tokai Kensetsu construction company.
